delta.name: Delta
delta.definition: The change in option value for a small change in the underlying price.
delta.interpretation: A call delta of 0.62 means the option gains about $0.62 when the stock gains $1 — and behaves, locally, like holding 0.62 shares. Calls live in (0, 1), puts in (−1, 0); at-the-money sits near ±0.5.
delta.business_meaning: Delta is the hedge ratio: sell delta-worth of stock against a long call and small moves cancel. Desks are typically required to run delta-neutral, so this is the number rebalanced all day.
delta.use_cases: Hedging, converting option positions into share-equivalents, and quoting conventions (a '25-delta put' names a strike by its delta).

gamma.name: Gamma
gamma.definition: The change in delta for a change in the underlying — the curvature of the value profile.
gamma.interpretation: High gamma means your hedge goes stale quickly: after a move you are no longer neutral. Gamma is always positive for long options, largest at-the-money near expiry.
gamma.business_meaning: Long gamma earns from realized movement (buy low, sell high while rebalancing) and pays theta for the privilege; short gamma is the reverse. The gamma/theta trade-off is the daily P&L story of every option book.
gamma.use_cases: Sizing hedge-rebalancing frequency, stress-testing large moves, understanding pin risk at expiry.

vega.name: Vega
vega.definition: The change in option value for a one-point change in implied volatility.
vega.interpretation: A vega of 0.38 means the option gains $0.38 if implied vol rises from 20% to 21%. Always positive for vanilla options; largest at-the-money and for longer maturities.
vega.business_meaning: Vega is exposure to the market's *opinion* about future turbulence, separate from any actual move in spot. Volatility trading is, concretely, the trading of vega.
vega.use_cases: Managing books through earnings/events, structuring straddles and strangles, marking exposure to the smile.

theta.name: Theta
theta.definition: The change in option value from one day passing, all else frozen.
theta.interpretation: Usually negative for long options: a theta of −0.02 means the position bleeds about two cents overnight if nothing happens. Decay accelerates near expiry for at-the-money strikes.
theta.business_meaning: Theta is the rent paid for optionality — the exact counterpart of gamma's earnings. A book's theta tells you what silence costs.
theta.use_cases: Income strategies (short premium), timing entries, and sanity-checking that gamma earned justifies theta paid.

rho.name: Rho
rho.definition: The change in option value for a one-point move in the risk-free rate.
rho.interpretation: Calls gain when rates rise (paying the strike later is cheaper in present-value terms); puts lose. Small for short-dated options, material for long-dated ones.
rho.business_meaning: Usually the quietest Greek on an equity desk — until rates move fast, or the product is long-dated, at which point ignored rho becomes unexplained P&L.
rho.use_cases: Long-dated options, LEAPS, convertibles, and any environment of rapid central-bank repricing.

yield_to_maturity.name: Yield to Maturity
yield_to_maturity.definition: The single discount rate that reprices the bond exactly to its market (here: curve-implied) price.
yield_to_maturity.interpretation: A one-number summary of the return locked in by buying at this price and holding to maturity — if all coupons reinvest at y, which they rarely do exactly.
yield_to_maturity.business_meaning: The industry's common denominator for comparing bonds of different coupons and maturities; the x-axis on which duration and convexity are defined.
yield_to_maturity.use_cases: Relative value across bonds, quoting, and as the anchor rate for all yield-based risk measures below.

macaulay_duration.name: Macaulay Duration
macaulay_duration.definition: The present-value-weighted average time at which the bond pays you.
macaulay_duration.interpretation: A 5-year bullet bond with coupons has Macaulay duration a bit under 5: the coupons pull the average arrival of your money earlier. For a zero coupon bond it equals maturity exactly.
macaulay_duration.business_meaning: The original 1938 meaning of 'duration' — the bond's center of gravity in time. Useful for immunization: match your assets' duration to your liabilities' and small parallel rate moves wash out.
macaulay_duration.use_cases: Liability-driven investing, immunization, and as the stepping stone to modified duration.

modified_duration.name: Modified Duration
modified_duration.definition: The percentage price sensitivity to a small parallel change in yield.
modified_duration.interpretation: Modified duration 4.3 means: yields up 1% ⇒ price down roughly 4.3%. The 'roughly' is what convexity corrects.
modified_duration.business_meaning: The single most used number in fixed income risk — the bond-market equivalent of delta.
modified_duration.use_cases: Portfolio duration targeting, hedging with futures/swaps, quick P&L estimates on rate moves.

convexity.name: Convexity
convexity.definition: The curvature of the price–yield relationship — how duration itself changes as yields move.
convexity.interpretation: Positive convexity is the pleasant asymmetry of plain bonds: prices rise more when yields fall than they drop when yields rise by the same amount. The duration estimate under-predicts gains and over-predicts losses.
convexity.business_meaning: Convexity is worth paying for in volatile rate environments — and is exactly what callable bonds give away (their convexity turns negative near the call).
convexity.use_cases: Second-order P&L attribution, barbell-vs-bullet trades, evaluating callable and mortgage-backed structures.

dv01.name: DV01 / PVBP
dv01.definition: The dollar value of one basis point: the currency change in price for a 0.01% move in yield.
dv01.interpretation: A DV01 of $430 on a $1m position means each basis point of yield moves the position by about $430.
dv01.business_meaning: The trading floor's native rates unit. Positions, hedges, and limits are stated in DV01 because it adds up linearly across a book.
dv01.use_cases: Hedge sizing ('sell futures to flatten 12k of DV01'), risk limits, and cross-instrument rate hedging.

pv01.name: PV01
pv01.unit: currency per 1bp of the fixed rate
pv01.definition: The value of one basis point on the fixed leg: notional times the annuity factor times 0.0001.
pv01.interpretation: A PV01 of $455 means each basis point added to the fixed rate moves the fixed leg's PV by about $455 — equivalently, how much a 1bp mis-strike of the swap rate is worth.
pv01.business_meaning: The swap desk's sizing unit. Because it is built from the annuity, it also converts rate spreads into money: value ≈ PV01 × (par − fixed) in basis points.
pv01.use_cases: Sizing swap hedges, quoting, converting basis-point spreads to P&L.

npv.name: Net Present Value
npv.definition: The signed current worth of the position: everything you expect to receive minus everything you expect to pay, discounted.
npv.interpretation: A new at-market swap has NPV ≈ 0 by construction; NPV drifts away from zero as the curve moves after inception.
npv.business_meaning: The mark-to-market — what the position would settle for today, and the number collateral calls are made on.
npv.use_cases: Daily P&L, collateral/margin calculation, unwind pricing.

par_rate.name: Par Swap Rate
par_rate.definition: The fixed rate that makes the swap worth exactly zero at inception.
par_rate.interpretation: If the par rate is 3.96% and you pay fixed 4.00%, you overpay by 4bp per period — the swap's negative NPV is that overpayment times the annuity.
par_rate.business_meaning: The rate actually quoted on screens: swap markets trade par rates, and the NPV of any seasoned swap is the drift between its locked rate and today's par rate.
par_rate.use_cases: Quoting, curve building (par swaps are bootstrap inputs), relative value.

cs01.name: CS01 (Spread DV01)
cs01.definition: The change in CDS value when the market spread moves one basis point wider.
cs01.interpretation: Positive for a protection buyer (wider spreads mean your insurance got more valuable), negative for a seller. Roughly the risky annuity times notional times 1bp.
cs01.business_meaning: The credit desk's DV01: positions, hedges, and limits on a CDS book are all stated in CS01.
cs01.use_cases: Hedging bond credit risk with CDS, sizing curve trades, daily credit P&L attribution.

recovery01.name: Recovery Sensitivity
recovery01.definition: The change in CDS value if the assumed recovery rate rises one percentage point.
recovery01.interpretation: Subtle: higher recovery shrinks the loss paid on default but also raises the implied hazard needed to match the same market spread. Near par the effects largely cancel; off-market they don't.
recovery01.business_meaning: Recovery is the least observable input in credit — this measure quantifies how much that ignorance costs.
recovery01.use_cases: Stress testing distressed names, recovery-swap pricing, model risk assessment.

default_probability.name: Default Probability
default_probability.definition: The risk-neutral probability that the reference entity defaults before maturity.
default_probability.interpretation: A 5y CDS at 100bp with 40% recovery implies roughly an 8% chance of default within five years — risk-neutral, so typically above the real-world frequency by a risk premium.
default_probability.business_meaning: The translation of spreads into the language of probability — how credit committees and regulators actually think.
default_probability.use_cases: Counterparty risk (CVA inputs), comparing market-implied vs rating-agency default rates, limit setting.

implied_hazard_rate.name: Implied Hazard Rate
implied_hazard_rate.definition: The default intensity implied by the market spread via the credit triangle.
implied_hazard_rate.interpretation: Conditional on having survived so far, the annualized instantaneous default rate. 95bp at 40% recovery ⇒ λ ≈ 1.58%.
implied_hazard_rate.business_meaning: The one-number summary of how the market prices this name's raw default risk, stripped of recovery.
implied_hazard_rate.use_cases: Curve building, relative value across names, feeding survival probabilities into XVA systems.

fx_delta.name: FX Delta
fx_delta.unit: domestic currency per unit of spot FX
fx_delta.definition: The change in position value for a one-unit move in the spot exchange rate.
fx_delta.interpretation: For a forward buying €1m, roughly €1m·e^{-r_f T} dollars of exposure per unit of EURUSD — slightly under the notional because foreign cash earns interest until delivery.
fx_delta.business_meaning: The hedge ratio for FX risk: sell this much spot against the forward and small currency moves cancel.
fx_delta.use_cases: FX hedging, aggregating currency exposure across forwards and swaps, treasury risk reports.

spot_delta.name: Spot Delta
spot_delta.unit: currency per unit of spot price
spot_delta.definition: The change in the futures position's value for a one-unit move in the spot commodity price.
spot_delta.interpretation: Close to the quantity held, scaled by the carry gross-up: a long 1,000-barrel position has roughly 1,000 barrels of spot exposure.
spot_delta.business_meaning: Connects paper positions to physical exposure — what a producer's hedge actually offsets.
spot_delta.use_cases: Producer/consumer hedging programs, basis risk monitoring, inventory-vs-futures books.

inflation01.name: Inflation DV01
inflation01.definition: The change in the linker's value when breakeven inflation rises one basis point.
inflation01.interpretation: Always positive for a long linker: higher expected inflation grows every indexed cash flow. The nominal-curve DV01 alongside it captures the rates leg; together they span the linker's two-factor risk.
inflation01.business_meaning: The breakeven trade in one number: long linker + short nominal bond isolates exactly this exposure.
inflation01.use_cases: Breakeven trading, inflation-hedging pension liabilities, real-vs-nominal asset allocation.
